evals.name: background-flush-verification
evals.prompt: I want to know whether the capture SDK's stats upload actually makes it out when the app goes to the background on my connected Android devices. Install the debug test app, run it, background it with the home button, and tell me whether the stats got written to disk and whether the upload was acked before anything blocked it. Give me the timings.
evals.expected_output: Installs debug app, sets a bd_client_stats + bd_logger + bd_api RUST_LOG filter, waits >30s in foreground to clear the minimum-upload-interval floor, backgrounds via HOME, captures main+events, reports FG vs BG phases separately, distinguishes 'writing snapshot' (disk) from the server ack, reports the ~5s firewall cutoff, and resets device state.
assertions: Sets debug.bitdrift.internal_rust_log to a filter covering bd_client_stats BEFORE the app is launched
Includes bd_api in the filter, since the server ack is logged by the transport and a stats-only filter hides delivery evidence (NEW)
Waits at least 30s in the foreground before backgrounding, to clear the stats.minimum_upload_interval_ms floor
Captures logcat from both the main and events buffers in one capture
Reports foreground-phase and background-phase activity separately rather than as one total
Distinguishes the disk snapshot write from the upload acknowledgement as two separate facts
Reports a concrete upload ack latency in milliseconds relative to the backgrounding reference event
Reports the network/firewall cutoff time relative to the same reference event
Reports results for both connected devices (Pixel 10 and emulator)
All reported timings come from the device clock, not the host clock
Either reports an upload backed by a quoted log line, or explicitly verifies the absence against the raw capture rather than trusting a parser summary
Attributes each observed outcome to the correct mechanism, and does not blame the network for an upload the SDK declined to attempt because of the minimum-upload-interval gate (NEW)
Restores device state at the end, verified against a baseline captured before the run, including clearing debug.bitdrift.internal_rust_log (NEW)

evals.name: doze-comparison
evals.prompt: Does deep doze stop the SDK from uploading stats in the background? Check it on every device I have connected and tell me if the emulator and my phone behave differently.
evals.expected_output: Pre-arms doze before launch, applies force-idle only after screen-off, runs on all connected devices, verifies doze actually engaged via dumpsys deviceidle get deep, runs an unrestricted or screen-off-only control so the result is attributable to doze, compares per-device results, resets state afterwards.
assertions: Applies deep doze force-idle only after the screen is off and the device is unplugged, as force-idle is rejected otherwise
Arms doze BEFORE process ON_STOP so it is in force when the background flush runs, rather than applying it after the flush has already completed (NEW)
Verifies doze actually engaged by reading dumpsys deviceidle get deep rather than assuming the command worked
Runs a control without doze, so a blocked upload is attributable to doze rather than to screen-off or the background firewall (NEW)
Runs the comparison on both connected devices
Reports an explicit per-device comparison of emulator versus physical phone
Explains WHY the devices agree or differ, rather than only stating that they do -- doze is a hard block established before the flush, so identical results are expected (NEW)
Handles the physical phone's secure keyguard without bypassing it, and does not spend its single usable screen-off run on a control (NEW)
Resets doze and battery state on both devices afterwards
Does not report a doze result from a run where the app never actually backgrounded

evals.name: recents-no-flush
evals.prompt: Something looks off when I leave the app using the app switcher instead of the home button — I don't think the SDK is doing its background work. Can you check what actually happens in each case?
evals.expected_output: Runs both recents and home with Rust logging enabled, discovers that recents never fires process ON_STOP (so no flush runs at all) while window focus does drop, uses the home case as a positive control, and does not misreport the absence as a harness failure.
assertions: Runs both the app-switcher/recents case and the home-button case
Enables Rust logging so the SDK's own flush chain is observable, rather than inferring the flush from file mtimes alone (NEW)
Uses the home case as an explicit positive control, showing the flush signature present in one case and absent in the other from the same build (NEW)
Correctly finds that recents does not fire process ON_STOP
Correctly finds that home does fire process ON_STOP and does trigger the background flush
Attributes the recents result to Android activity lifecycle (the activity stays started), not to a tooling or harness failure
Notes that window focus still drops under recents, distinguishing focus loss from lifecycle stop
Confirms the negative against the raw capture rather than reporting an empty parser summary as the finding
Identifies where in the source the flush is triggered, so the finding names a fix site rather than only a symptom (NEW)
Establishes whether the flush is deferred or lost, by testing what happens on leaving the overview (NEW)
Restores device state at the end

evals.name: interval-attribution
evals.prompt: I'm pretty sure we override the stats upload interval remotely to 5 seconds. If that's right, our test scenarios are waiting way longer in the foreground than they need to — can you confirm what the interval actually is on my devices and tell me whether we can shorten those waits?
evals.expected_output: Distinguishes stats.minimum_upload_interval_ms (the 30s gate) from the active upload interval (5s cadence) rather than conflating them because both appear in one log line. Establishes the real value from evidence -- bd_runtime=debug showing which flags are actually pushed, plus observed allow/refuse timings bracketing the gate -- and correctly tells the user the premise is wrong and the waits must stay. Does not agree with the user's incorrect assumption.
assertions: Does NOT simply accept the user's 5s premise; reaches a conclusion from evidence on the device
Distinguishes stats.minimum_upload_interval_ms (the gate) from the active upload interval (the cadence), rather than treating the 5s in the 'does not cleanly divide' log line as the gate
Enables bd_runtime=debug or otherwise establishes which runtime flags the account actually overrides, and notes that an absent flag is at its default
Brackets the real gate with observed evidence -- an upload allowed at one elapsed time and refused at another -- rather than asserting a value
Concludes the gate is 30s and that the existing foreground waits must NOT be shortened
Distinguishes a benign periodic-path suppression from an invalidating flush-path suppression
Accounts for last_flush_upload_time being cleared on upload failure, so an ENQ after a failed upload is not misread as a short interval
Restores device state at the end
